title: New Zealand cultural participation rises while active creation falls and digital tools reshape production
source_unit: Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage, New Zealanders’ Cultural Participation in 2025, Verian survey research
geography: New Zealand; adults aged 18 years and over, with selected age, ethnicity, creator, and volunteer comparisons

observations.period: 2022, 2023, and 2025; arts, culture, and heritage participation and active creation

denominator.unit: New Zealand adults aged 18 years and over surveyed online by Verian in September–October 2025; weighted population estimates and prior-wave comparisons

attendance_2025.unit: percent visiting or attending at least one arts, culture, or heritage activity in the previous 12 months

attendance_2023.unit: percent visiting or attending at least one activity in the previous 12 months

attendance_2022.unit: percent visiting or attending at least one activity in the previous 12 months

creation_2025.unit: percent actively creating, performing, or producing cultural or creative work in the previous 12 months

creation_2023.unit: percent actively creating, performing, or producing cultural or creative work in the previous 12 months

access_convenience_enabler.unit: percent identifying accessibility or convenience—including price, location, transport, parking, or timing—as a factor that would encourage more engagement

attendance_creation_tension.value: attendance rose from 81% in 2022 to 88% in 2025 while active creation fell from 44% in 2023 to 40% in 2025

mechanism.value: Cultural life has separate audience and creator conversion stages: broad attendance recovery can coexist with less active production and persistent access friction

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Manatū Taonga’s 2025 cultural-participation research summary, with comparisons to the 2022 and 2023 waves. The 2025 research used a weighted online Verian panel of 2,000 adults.
observations.uncertainty: This is commissioned online-panel survey research, not administrative attendance or creator records. Cross-wave comparisons may reflect survey mode, sample, wording, weighting, recall, and activity-definition changes; the survey does not establish causal effects of cost, access, transport, time, or technology.
observations.subgroup: New Zealand adults aged 18 years and over, with selected activity, creator, and access measures.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher reported attendance may reflect post-pandemic normalization, while lower active creation may reflect definition or sample changes; an access/convenience response is a stated enabler, not observed price sensitivity or participation conversion.

observations.period: 2025; digital creation, generative AI, and cultural volunteering

denominator.unit: New Zealand adults aged 18 years and over surveyed online by Verian; creator and volunteer subgroups are nested within the published survey frame

digital_tool_creators.unit: percent of New Zealand adults represented by creators who use digital tools; equivalent to 69% of creators

generative_ai_creator_users.unit: percent of creators who use digital tools and specifically used generative AI in their creative process

genai_idea_use.unit: percent of creator digital-tool users using generative AI to explore or improve ideas

genai_generate_work.unit: percent of creator digital-tool users using generative AI to generate or produce work

nonuser_skill_barrier.unit: percent of creators who do not use digital tools identifying lack of technological skills or knowledge as a barrier

cultural_volunteering.unit: percent of New Zealand adults volunteering to support arts, culture, or heritage activities

volunteer_age_ethnicity_gradient.value: 35% among ages 18-29 versus 21% among people over 30; 31% among Māori versus 23% among non-Māori

mechanism.value: Cultural production is being reorganized through selective digital and generative-AI use while volunteer labor remains a social-infrastructure input; skill gaps may shape who can convert tools into cultural output

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the 2025 survey’s new digital-technology and volunteering modules; subgroup percentages are reported by the Ministry and refer to creators or volunteers where specified.
observations.uncertainty: The survey measures self-reported use and volunteering, not verified outputs, quality, income, copyright, labor substitution, or organizational dependence. Because the sample is an online panel, people with lower digital capability may be underrepresented; subgroup differences are descriptive and noncausal.
observations.subgroup: New Zealand creators, digital-tool users, nonusers, volunteers, age groups, and Māori/non-Māori respondents within the adult survey frame.
observations.counterinterpretation: Generative-AI use can mean experimentation rather than replacement or productivity; volunteering rates do not establish hours, retention, organizational value, or unequal burden.

boundary: This record adds a New Zealand cultural audience/creator/digital/volunteer layer. It does not establish causal access effects, creator earnings, AI productivity, copyright outcomes, cultural quality, wellbeing impact, or representative subgroup trajectories beyond the survey’s weighted online-panel frame.
